drivingQuestion: In what ratio of permitted food is a forbidden food nullified, and may that ratio be derived from the cooked foreleg of the nazirite's ram?
outcomeNote: The sixty-versus-one-hundred measure is never decided: Abaye, Rava and Ravina each give a different account of the baraita's restrictive זהו, the derivation from the nazirite's foreleg is twice blocked as a חידוש and twice rescued as a stringency, Rav Dimi is silenced over the leaven clause and then rescued by Abaye, and the unit closes only by explaining why brine is a special case.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן?
segments.en: Abaye «said to him: Here we are dealing with»

segments.he: בְּבֵיצַת אֶפְרוֹחַ, אֲבָל טְמֵאָה – לָא.
segments.en: «an egg» that contains «a chick,» as the chick imparts flavor to the food in which the egg is cooked. «But» with regard to an egg that does not contain a chick but is from «a non-kosher» bird, it does «not» impart flavor to the food with which it is cooked.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: בֵּיצִים טְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁשְּׁלָקָן עִם בֵּיצִים טְמֵאוֹת, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם – כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת. הָכָא נָמֵי בְּבֵיצַת אֶפְרוֹחַ, וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לַהּ ״טְמֵאָה״? כֵּיוָן דְּאִית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ, קָרֵי לַהּ ״טְמֵאָה״.
segments.en: Rav Idi bar Avin «raised an objection to» this answer based on a baraita (Tosefta, Terumot 9:5): With regard to «kosher eggs that one boiled with non-kosher eggs, if they have» a ratio that allows the non-kosher eggs to «impart flavor» to the kosher eggs, «they are all forbidden.» This indicates that eggs from non-kosher birds do have flavor. Abaye answered: «Here, too» it is referring «to an egg» from a kosher bird that contains «a chick. And why» does the baraita «call this a non-kosher» egg, indicating that it is an egg from a non-kosher species? «Since it has a chick inside,» which causes the egg to be forbidden, the baraita «calls it non-kosher.»

segments.he: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: בֵּיצִים שֶׁשְּׁלָקָן וְנִמְצָא אֶפְרוֹחַ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם – כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא דְּלֵית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ עָסְקִינַן.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But from» the fact «that the latter clause teaches:» With regard to «eggs that one boiled and a chick was found in one of them, if they have» a ratio that allows the chick to «impart flavor to them, they are all forbidden, it may be inferred that» in «the first clause we are dealing with» an egg «that does not have a chick inside.»

segments.he: פָּירוּשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ: בֵּיצִים טְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁשְּׁלָקָן עִם בֵּיצִים טְמֵאוֹת, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם – כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת. כֵּיצַד? כְּגוֹן שֶׁשְּׁלָקָן וְנִמְצָא אֶפְרוֹחַ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן.
segments.en: The Gemara explains that this is an incorrect inference, as the latter clause «is explaining» the first clause, so that the baraita should be read as follows: With regard to «kosher eggs that one boiled with non-kosher eggs, if they have» a ratio that allows the non-kosher eggs to «impart flavor» to the kosher eggs, «they are all forbidden. How» so? It can be referring to a case «where one boiled them and a chick was found in one of them.»

segments.he: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רֵישָׁא דְּלֵית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ – הַשְׁתָּא דְּלֵית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ אֲסוּרָה, דְּאִית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ מִיבַּעְיָא?
segments.en: The Gemara adds: «So too it is reasonable» to explain the baraita in this manner, «as if» it would «enter your mind» to say that «the first clause» is referring to a case «where there is no chick in» the egg, the latter clause is redundant: «Now» that the tanna has taught that in a case «where there is no chick inside,» the non-kosher egg imparts flavor to the kosher eggs and renders them «forbidden, is» it «necessary» for the tanna to teach that an egg «that has a chick inside» imparts flavor to the kosher eggs?

segments.he: אִי מִשּׁוּם הָא לָא אִירְיָא, תְּנָא סֵיפָא לְגַלּוֹיֵי רֵישָׁא, שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאמַר: רֵישָׁא – דְּאִית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ, אֲבָל לֵית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ – שַׁרְיָא, תְּנָא סֵיפָא דְּאִית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא דְּלֵית בַּהּ אֶפְרוֹחַ, וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי אֲסִירָא.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this argument: «If it is due to that» reason, «there is no» conclusive «argument,» i.e., the proof of the argument is inconclusive. The reason is that one can say that the tanna «taught the latter clause to reveal» the meaning of «the first clause.» The latter clause was stated so «that you would not» mistakenly «say» that «the first clause» is referring only to a case «where» the egg «has a chick inside, but» if «there is no chick inside» the kosher eggs would be «permitted.» Therefore, the tanna «teaches the latter clause» and specifies «that» it is referring to an egg «that has a chick inside. By inference the first clause» is referring to a case of an egg «that does not have a chick inside, and even so it» renders all of the other eggs «forbidden.»

segments.he: הָהוּא כְּזֵיתָא תַּרְבָּא דִּנְפַל בְּדִיקּוּלָא דְּבִשְׂרָא, סָבַר רַב אַסִּי לְשַׁעוֹרֵיהּ בְּמַאי דִּבְלַע דִּיקּוּלָא, אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַטּוּ דְּהֶיתֵּרָא בָּלַע, דְּאִיסּוּרָא לָא בָּלַע?
segments.en: § The Gemara continues discussing the nullification of forbidden foods. There was once «a certain olive-bulk» of forbidden «fat that fell into a pot of» kosher «meat. Rav Asi thought to measure» the volume of the kosher meat together «with that which the pot had absorbed. The Rabbis said to Rav Ashi: Is that to say that» the pot «absorbed» the «permitted» meat but «did not absorb» the «forbidden» fat?

segments.he: הָהוּא פַּלְגָא דְּזֵיתָא דְּתַרְבָּא דִּנְפַל בְּדִיקּוּלָא דְּבִשְׂרָא, סָבַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי לְשַׁעוֹרֵיהּ בִּתְלָתִין פַּלְגֵי דְּזֵיתָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֲבוּהּ: לָאו אָמֵינָא לָךְ לָא תְּזַלְזֵל בְּשִׁיעוּרִין דְּרַבָּנַן? וְעוֹד, הָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲצִי שִׁיעוּר אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara relates a similar incident: There was once «a certain half-olive-bulk of» forbidden «fat that fell into a pot of» kosher «meat. Mar bar Rav Ashi thought to measure» the amount of kosher meat needed to nullify the forbidden fat as «thirty half-olive-bulks,» rather than sixty. «His father,» Rav Ashi, «said to him: Have I not told you: Do not» treat «measures lightly» even with regard to «rabbinic» prohibitions? «And furthermore, didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: A half-measure» is «prohibited by Torah» law? Consequently, the half-olive-bulk of forbidden fat is nullified only in sixty times its volume of permitted meat.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אִידִי בַּר גֵּרְשֹׁם, אָמַר לֵוִי בַּר פְּרָטָא, אָמַר רַבִּי נַחוּם, אָמַר רַבִּי בִּירְיָים מִשּׁוּם זָקֵן אֶחָד, וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמֵיהּ, דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה אָמְרוּ: בֵּיצָה בְּשִׁשִּׁים – אֲסוּרָה, בְּשִׁשִּׁים וְאַחַת – מוּתֶּרֶת.
segments.en: § The Gemara continues its discussion of nullifying forbidden foods. «Rav Shemen bar Abba says» that «Rav Idi bar Idi bar Gershom says» that «Levi bar Perata says» that «Rabbi Naḥum says» that «Rabbi Biryam says in the name of a certain elder, and his name was Rabbi Ya’akov,» that the Sages «in the house of the Nasi said:» If a non-kosher «egg» is mixed «with» kosher eggs, if there are «sixty» eggs they are all «forbidden,» but if there are «sixty-one» eggs they «are» all «permitted.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא: רְאֵה שֶׁאַתָּה מֵטִיל בָּהּ גְּבוּל הֶיתֵּר, שֶׁהֲרֵי שְׁנֵי גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר לֹא פֵּירְשׁוּ אֶת הַדָּבָר. רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי, תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי: בֵּיצָה בְּשִׁשִּׁים – אֲסוּרָה, בְּשִׁשִּׁים וְאַחַת – מוּתֶּרֶת.
segments.en: «Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Shemen bar Abba: See,» one can infer from your words «that you fix a limit» to «permit» the eggs if there is a total of sixty-one eggs, including the non-kosher egg. This is a revelation, «because the two» most «eminent» Sages «of the generation did not clarify this matter.» These two eminent Sages were «Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi and Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani,» and «both of them said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:» In a case where a non-kosher «egg» is mixed «with» kosher eggs, if there are «sixty» eggs they are all «forbidden,» but if there are «sixty-one» eggs they «are» all «permitted.»

segments.he: וְאִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּשִׁשִּׁים וְאַחַת, בַּהֲדֵי דִּידַהּ, אוֹ דִילְמָא לְבַר מִינַּהּ? וְלָא פְּשׁוּט, וּמָר פָּשֵׁיט לַהּ מִפְשָׁט.
segments.en: «And a dilemma was raised before» these Sages: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said they are permitted if there are «sixty-one» eggs, does that mean there are «sixty-one» eggs altogether, «with the» non-kosher egg, «or» does it «perhaps» mean that there must be sixty-one kosher eggs «aside from» the non-kosher egg? «And» they «did not resolve» this dilemma. «And» yet, it appears as though «the Master,» Rav Shemen, has «resolved» the dilemma, because you implied that the mixture is kosher if there are a total of sixty-one eggs including the non-kosher egg.

segments.he: אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בֵּיצָה בְּשִׁשִּׁים וְהִיא – אֲסוּרָה, בְּשִׁשִּׁים וְאַחַת וְהִיא – מוּתֶּרֶת.
segments.en: The Gemara continues: It «was stated» that «Rabbi Ḥelbo says» that «Rav Huna says:» If a non-kosher «egg» becomes mixed «with» kosher eggs, if there are «sixty» kosher eggs in addition to «that» non-kosher egg, the entire mixture is «forbidden.» But if there are «sixty-one» kosher eggs in addition to «that» one non-kosher egg, the mixture is «permitted.»

segments.he: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַבָּא לֹא שִׁיעֵר בְּאַרְבָּעִים וָשֶׁבַע, וַאֲנִי אֲשַׁעֵר בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְחָמֵשׁ.
segments.en: § There was «a certain» person «who came before Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi with a half-olive-bulk of non-kosher food that had been mixed with a larger amount of kosher food. Rabban Gamliel «said to him:» A similar case came before my «father,» and even though he «did not measure» the kosher food as being sixty times the volume of the non-kosher food, he nevertheless permitted the mixture due to the fact that there was «forty-seven» times as much kosher food as non-kosher food. «And» similarly, «I will» permit the mixture because I «measure» that the kosher food is «forty-five» times the volume of the non-kosher food.

segments.he: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַבָּא לֹא שִׁיעֵר בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְחָמֵשׁ, וַאֲנִי אֲשַׁעֵר בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ.
segments.en: Similarly there was «a certain» person «who came before Rabbi Shimon bar Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi with a mixture of kosher and non-kosher food. Rabbi Shimon «said to him:» A similar case came before my «father,» and even though he «did not measure» the kosher food as being sixty times the volume of the non-kosher food, he nevertheless permitted the mixture due to the fact that there was «forty-five» times as much kosher food as non-kosher food. «And» similarly, «I will» permit the mixture because I «measure» that the kosher food is «forty-three» times the volume of the non-kosher food.

segments.he: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ שְׁלֹשִׁים?
segments.en: There was «a certain» man «who came before Rabbi Ḥiyya» with a mixture of kosher and non-kosher food. Rabbi Ḥiyya «said to him: Is there» even «thirty» times the volume of permitted food as forbidden food? Clearly, the mixture is forbidden.

segments.he: טַעְמָא דְּלֵיכָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים, הָא אִיכָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים – מְשַׁעֲרִין? אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: גּוּזְמָא.
segments.en: The Gemara seeks to clarify: This indicates that «the reason» that he prohibited the mixture is «that there was not thirty» times as much kosher food as non-kosher food. «But» it may then be inferred that if «there is thirty» times as much kosher food as non-kosher food, one may «assess,» i.e., permit, the mixture. And this contradicts the halakha that non-kosher food is nullified only in a mixture containing sixty times as much kosher food as non-kosher food. «Rabbi Ḥanina said:» Rabbi Ḥiyya did not make this statement to set a halakhic principle, but merely as «an exaggeration.» There was not even thirty times the volume of kosher food, so it was obvious that the mixture was forbidden.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא: כָּל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְּשִׁשִּׁים. אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: רַבִּי, אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן? הָכִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא: כָּל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְּמֵאָה!
segments.en: § «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says in the name of bar Kappara: All» the «forbidden» foods «in the Torah» are nullified when they are mixed «with» kosher food that is «sixty» times their volume. «Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said before» Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba: «My teacher, you say this» citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who said that bar Kappara said it. But «this is what Rav Asi says» that «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says in the name of bar Kappara: All» the «forbidden» foods «in the Torah» are nullified when they are mixed «with» kosher food that is «one hundred» times their volume.

segments.he: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מִ״זְּרוֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה״, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַזְּרֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה וְגוֹ׳״, וְתַנְיָא: ״בְּשֵׁלָה״ –
segments.en: The Gemara adds: «And both of them learned» their principles of nullification «only from» the term: «“Cooked foreleg,” as it is written» with regard to the nazirite’s ram: «“And the priest shall take the cooked foreleg» of the ram” (Numbers 6:19). «And it is taught» in a baraita: The verse states: «“Cooked,”»

segments.he: אֵין ״בְּשֵׁלָה״ אֶלָּא שְׁלֵימָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר: אֵין ״בְּשֵׁלָה״ אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלָה עִם הָאַיִל.
segments.en: and the term «“cooked”» indicates that the verse is referring «only» to a foreleg that is «whole. Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai» disagrees and «says:» The term «“cooked”» indicates that the verse is referring «only» to a foreleg «that is cooked with the» entire «ram.»

segments.he: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בַּהֲדֵי אַיִל מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ, מָר סָבַר: מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ, וּמָר סָבַר: מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara clarifies their dispute: «Everyone» agrees that «one cooks» the foreleg «with the» rest of the «ram.» But one «Sage holds» that one first «cuts» the foreleg off the animal «and then cooks it» along with the rest of the animal. «And» one «Sage,» Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai, «holds» that one first «cooks» the entire ram «and then cuts» off the foreleg.

segments.he: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ, מִיהוּ מָר סָבַר: בַּהֲדֵי אַיִל מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ, וּמָר סָבַר: בִּקְדֵרָה אַחֶרֶת מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ.
segments.en: «And if you wish, say that everyone» agrees that one first «cuts» off the foreleg «and then cooks it. But» one «Sage,» Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai, «holds» that one «cooks» the foreleg «with» the rest of «the ram, and» one «Sage holds» that he «cooks» the foreleg «in another pot,» separate from the rest of the ram.

segments.he: לְלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא – אַלִּיבָּא דְּדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל, לְלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא – אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי.
segments.en: The foreleg of the nazirite’s ram is permitted to be eaten only by a priest, whereas the rest of the ram is eaten by the nazirite even if he is not a priest. Consequently, «according to the first formulation, all agree» that the principle of nullification may be derived from here, since all agree that the foreleg is cooked together with the rest of the ram, and yet it does not cause the rest of the ram to be forbidden to a non-priest. «According to the latter formulation,» the principle of nullification may be derived from here «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai,» who says that the foreleg is cooked together with the rest of the ram. But according to the latter formulation the first tanna holds that the foreleg is not cooked with the rest of the ram, in which case the principle of nullification cannot be derived from here.

segments.he: מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּשִׁשִּׁים, סָבַר: בָּשָׂר וַעֲצָמוֹת בַּהֲדֵי בָּשָׂר וַעֲצָמוֹת מְשַׁעֲרִינַן, וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ בְּשִׁשִּׁים. מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּמֵאָה, סָבַר: בָּשָׂר בַּהֲדֵי בָּשָׂר מְשַׁעֲרִינַן, וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ בְּמֵאָה.
segments.en: The Gemara now returns to the dispute about whether non-kosher food is nullified in sixty or one hundred times its volume of kosher food, and explains how each opinion is derived from the halakha of the foreleg of the nazirite’s ram. «The one who said» that non-kosher food is nullified «in sixty» times its volume of kosher food «holds» that «we assess» the ratio of «meat and bones» of the foreleg «to» the «meat and bones» of the rest of the ram, «and this is» a ratio of one to «sixty. The one who said» that non-kosher food is nullified «in one hundred» times its volume of kosher food «holds» that «we assess» only the volume of the «meat» of the foreleg «to» the «meat» of the rest of the ram, «and this is» a ratio of one «to one hundred.»

segments.he: וּמִי יָלְפִינַן מִינַּהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא: זֶהוּ הֶיתֵּר הַבָּא מִכְּלַל אִיסּוּר, ״זֶהוּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? לָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי כׇּל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And do we derive» the principles of nullification «from» the case of the nazirite’s ram? «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita with regard to the nazirite’s ram, which absorbs the flavor of the foreleg with which it was cooked: «This is» a case of «permitted» meat «that comes from the category» of «forbidden» food, i.e., it is permitted despite the fact that it was cooked with forbidden food. The Gemara infers: «What» does the expression: «This is,» in the baraita serve «to exclude?» Does it «not» serve «to exclude all» the other «forbidden» foods «that are in the Torah?» This indicates that only the cooked foreleg of the nazirite’s ram is nullified in sixty or one hundred times its volume of permitted food, but other prohibited foods are not subject to the principle of nullification.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּהָכָא בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: The Gemara answers that «Abaye said:» This emphasis «is necessary only according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, who said» that in general, «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type is not nullified.» Therefore the baraita «teaches us that here,» the flavor imparted by the foreleg to the rest of the nazirite’s ram is «nullified.»

segments.he: וְלִיגְמַר מִינֵּיהּ? גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא ״וְלָקַח מִדַּם הַפָּר וּמִדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר״, תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ וְלָא בָּטְלִי.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «Let» Rabbi Yehuda «learn from this» case that all forbidden food can be nullified when it is mixed with permitted food of its own type. The Gemara explains: «The Merciful One revealed» in the Torah: «“And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat» and put it upon the corners of the altar round about” (Leviticus 16:18). «Both of» these two bloods «are» mixed «with each other, and» although a bull has more blood than a goat has, the verse makes reference to the blood of the goat, indicating that it maintains its own identity and is «not nullified.»

segments.he: וּמַאי חָזֵית דְּגָמְרִינַן מֵהַאיְךְ, לִיגְמַר מֵהַאי? חִדּוּשׁ הוּא, וּמֵחִדּוּשׁ לָא גָּמְרִינַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And» according to Rabbi Yehuda, «what did you see that» caused «you» to «derive» a principle «from that» verse with regard to the blood of the bull and the blood of the goat? «Derive» a principle «from this» verse about the foreleg of the nazirite’s ram. The Gemara answers: The case of the nazirite’s ram «is a novelty,» because even when nullification does apply one may not nullify a forbidden food ab initio, whereas here one is supposed to cook the foreleg together with the rest of the ram; «and we do not learn» principles «from a novelty.»

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, לְמֵאָה וְשִׁשִּׁים נָמֵי לָא לִיגְמַר?
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «If so,» if Rabbi Yehuda does not consider the case of the nazirite’s ram a viable precedent for general halakhic principles, then «let him also not learn» from that case that when forbidden food is mixed with permitted food of a different type, it is nullified «in» either «one hundred or sixty» times its own volume. As discussed above, the two opinions in this regard are each based on the case of the nazirite’s ram.

segments.he: אַטּוּ אֲנַן לְקוּלָּא גָּמְרִינַן? לְחוּמְרָא גָּמְרִינַן, דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בְּרוּבָּא בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «Is that to say» that «we learn» that forbidden food is nullified in sixty or one hundred times its volume of permitted food as «a leniency? We learn it» only as «a stringency, as» if it were not for this derivation, we would say that «by Torah law» forbidden food «is nullified in» a mixture in which there is a simple «majority» of permitted food.

segments.he: רָבָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְטַעַם כְּעִיקָּר, דִּבְקָדָשִׁים אָסוּר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּהָכָא שָׁרֵי.
segments.en: «Rava stated» an alternative explanation of the term: This is, which appears in the baraita with regard to the nazirite’s ram: This limitation «is necessary only for» the principle that the halakhic status of the «flavor» of forbidden food is «like» that of its «substance.» If the flavor of «sacrificial» food is absorbed into another food, it renders that food «forbidden,» i.e., it is not nullified. Therefore, the baraita «teaches us that here,» in the case of the nazirite’s ram, the rest of the ram is «permitted» even to non-priests.

segments.he: וְלִיגְמַר מִינֵּיהּ? גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי חַטָּאת: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יִקְדָּשׁ״, לִהְיוֹת כָּמוֹהָ – שֶׁאִם פְּסוּלָה תִּפָּסֵל, וְאִם כְּשֵׁרָה תֵּאָכֵל כֶּחָמוּר שֶׁבָּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «Let» us «learn from» the case of the nazirite’s ram that the flavor of sacrificial food can be nullified. The Gemara explains: «The Merciful One revealed» in the Torah «with regard to the sin offering: “Whatever shall touch its flesh shall be holy”» (Leviticus 6:20). This teaches that the halakhic status of any food that touches and absorbs flavor from a sin offering «becomes like it, so» that «if» the sin offering «is disqualified,» this food «shall» also «be disqualified, and if» the sin offering is «valid,» this food may be «eaten in accordance with the stringencies» that apply to a sin offering.

segments.he: וּמַאי חָזֵית דְּגָמְרִינַן מֵהַאיְךְ, לִיגְמַר מֵהַאי? חִדּוּשׁ הוּא, וּמֵחִדּוּשׁ לָא גָּמְרִינַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And what did you see» to indicate «that we learn» the principle of nullification concerning sacrificial food «from that» verse of the sin offering? «Derive it» instead «from this» verse concerning the foreleg of the nazirite’s ram. The Gemara answers: «This» case of the nazirite’s ram «is a novelty, and we do not learn» principles «from a novelty.»

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, לְמֵאָה וְשִׁשִּׁים נָמֵי לָא לִיגְמַר? אַטּוּ אֲנַן לְקוּלָּא קָא גָמְרִינַן? לְחוּמְרָא קָא גָמְרִינַן, דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בְּרוּבָּא בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «If so,» if the case of the nazirite’s ram is not a viable precedent for general halakhic principles, then «one should also not learn» from that case that when forbidden food is mixed with permitted food of a different type, it is nullified in either «one hundred or sixty» times its own volume. As discussed above, the two opinions in this regard are both based on the case of the nazirite’s ram. The Gemara responds: «Is that to say» that «we learn» that forbidden food is nullified in sixty or one hundred times its volume of permitted food as «a leniency? We learn it» only as «a stringency, as» if it were not for this derivation, one would say that «by Torah law» forbidden food «is nullified in» a mixture in which there is a simple «majority» of permitted food.

segments.he: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ, דְּאָמַר: מְקוֹם חֲתָךְ בְּעָלְמָא אָסוּר, וְהָכָא שְׁרֵי.
segments.en: «Ravina said» an alternative explanation of the term: This is, that appears in the baraita with regard to the nazirite’s ram. This limitation «is necessary only for the place» where the foreleg is «cut» from the body of the ram, «as» it was «said» that in a case where permitted and forbidden foods were attached and one cut the forbidden section from the permitted section, «the place of the cut» on the permitted part «is generally forbidden. But here,» in the case of the nazirite’s ram, «it is permitted.»

segments.he: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי, וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to discussing the statement of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak (98a) that forbidden food is nullified in a mixture only if there is one hundred times its volume of permitted food. «Rav Dimi sat and said this halakha.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְכׇל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְּמֵאָה? וְהָתְנַן: לָמָה אָמְרוּ כׇּל הַמְחַמֵּץ וּמְתַבֵּל וּמְדַמֵּעַ לְהַחְמִיר – מִין וּמִינוֹ, לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר – מִין וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ.
segments.en: «Abaye said to him: And» is it true that «all the forbidden» foods «in the Torah» that are mixed with permitted foods are nullified only «in» a mixture containing «one hundred» times their volume of permitted food? «But didn’t we learn» in a mishna (Orla 2:6): «Why did» the Sages «say» that with regard to «anyone who leavens» non-sacred food with a leavening agent that is teruma «or flavors» it with spices of teruma «or mixes» teruma into non-sacred food, thereby making the food forbidden for non-priests, the halakha is «to be stringent» if he mixed one «type» of food that is teruma with non-sacred food of the same «type.» But the halakha is «to be lenient and to be stringent» if he mixed one «type» of teruma with non-sacred food of «a different type.»

segments.he: וְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר מִין וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, כֵּיצַד? גְּרִיסִין שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם הָעֲדָשִׁים, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בֵּין יֵשׁ בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, בֵּין אֵין בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד – אָסוּר.
segments.en: «And it is taught in the latter clause,» i.e., in the following mishna (Orla 2:7): When it is stated that the halakha is «to be lenient and to be stringent» if he mixed one «type» of teruma with non-sacred food «not» of «its type, how» is this accomplished? For example, in a case of «split beans» of teruma that were cooked «with» non-sacred «lentils, if there are» enough split beans relative to the lentils to «impart flavor» to the lentils, then regardless of «whether there are» enough lentils «to neutralize» the split beans «in one hundred and one» times their volume, i.e., the volume of the lentils is one hundred and one times the volume of the split beans, or «whether there are not» enough lentils «to neutralize» the split beans «in one hundred and one» times their volume, the entire mixture is «forbidden» to a non-priest.

segments.he: אֵין בָּהֶן בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, בֵּין אֵין בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד – מוּתָּר.
segments.en: Conversely, if «there are not» enough split beans of teruma to «impart flavor» to the lentils, then regardless of «whether there are» enough lentils «to neutralize» the split beans «in one hundred and one» times their volume, or «whether there are not» enough lentils «to neutralize» the split beans «in one hundred and one» times their volume, the mixture is «permitted» even to a non-priest.

segments.he: אֵין בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, אֶלָּא בְּמַאי? לָאו בְּשִׁשִּׁים?
segments.en: Abaye commented: When the mishna says that «there are not» enough lentils «to neutralize» the split beans «in one hundred and one» times their volume, and nevertheless if the split beans did not impart flavor to the lentils, the mixture is permitted, «in what» amount of lentils are the split beans nullified? Is it «not» that the split beans are permitted because they are mixed «with sixty» times their volume of non-sacred lentils? This contradicts the opinion of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak.

segments.he: לָא, בְּמֵאָה.
segments.en: Rav Dimi answered Abaye: «No,» the mishna means that although there is not one hundred and one times as much non-sacred food as teruma, the teruma is nullified because there is «one hundred» times its volume of non-sacred food.

segments.he: וְהָא מִדְּרֵישָׁא בְּמֵאָה הָוֵי, סֵיפָא בְּשִׁשִּׁים! דְּקָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא: לְהַחְמִיר מִין וּמִינוֹ כֵּיצַד? שְׂאוֹר שֶׁל חִטִּין שֶׁנָּפַל לְעִיסַּת חִטִּין, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, בֵּין יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, בֵּין אֵין בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד – אָסוּר.
segments.en: Abaye responded: «But since the first clause» states that it is nullified «in one hundred» times its volume, it must «be» that «the latter clause» is referring to a case where there is «sixty» times its volume. «As» the mishna (Orla 2:6) «teaches in the first clause:» When it is stated that the halakha is «to be stringent» if one «type» of teruma is mixed with non-sacred food of «its type, how» is this accomplished? For example, in a case of «leaven of» teruma «wheat that fell into dough» made of non-sacred «wheat, and there is enough» teruma «to cause» the non-sacred wheat «to become leavened, whether there is» enough non-sacred wheat «to neutralize» the teruma «in one hundred and one» times its volume, or «whether there is not» enough non-sacred wheat «to neutralize» the teruma «in one hundred and one» times its volume, the entire dough «is forbidden» to a non-priest.

segments.he: אֵין בּוֹ לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, בֵּין אֵין בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ – אָסוּר. רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא בִּמְאָה?
segments.en: But if «there is not» enough non-sacred wheat «to neutralize» the teruma «in one hundred and one» times its volume, then «whether there is» enough teruma «to cause» the non-sacred wheat «to become leavened» or «whether there is not» enough teruma «to cause» the non-sacred wheat «to become leavened,» the entire dough «is forbidden» to a non-priest. Would you suggest that both «the first clause and the latter clause» are stating that the teruma is nullified «in one hundred» times its volume?

segments.he: לָא, רֵישָׁא בִּמְאָה וְחַד, וְסֵיפָא בִּמְאָה.
segments.en: Rav Dimi answered: «No. The first clause» is referring to a case where the teruma is mixed «with one hundred and one» times its volume of non-sacred food, «and the latter clause» is referring to a case where the teruma is mixed «with one hundred» times its volume of non-sacred food.

segments.he: וְכִי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ בִּמְאָה וְחַד, אַמַּאי לָא בְּטִיל? אִישְׁתִּיק.
segments.en: Abaye asked Rav Dimi: If so, «when» the mishna states that if «there is» enough teruma «to cause» the non-sacred wheat «to become leavened» the entire mixture is forbidden to non-priests, why is that the case? If leaven is mixed «with one hundred and one» times its volume of non-sacred wheat it will have no leavening effect, so «why is it not nullified?» Rav Dimi did not have an answer and «was silent.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא שָׁאנֵי שְׂאוֹר דְּחִימּוּצוֹ קָשֶׁה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַדְכַּרְתַּן מִילְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לֹא כׇּל הַשִּׁיעוּרִין שָׁוִין, שֶׁהֲרֵי צִיר שִׁיעוּרוֹ קָרוֹב לְמָאתַיִם. דִּתְנַן: דָּג טָמֵא צִירוֹ אָסוּר, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רְבִיעִית בְּסָאתַיִם.
segments.en: Abaye «said to him: Perhaps leaven is different, because its leavening» properties are «potent,» and there are some forms of leaven that can have an effect on such a large quantity of dough. Rav Dimi «said to him: You reminded me» of «a matter that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: Not all the measures are equal, because the measure» required in order to nullify non-kosher fish «brine» is «close to two hundred» times its volume. «As we learned» in a mishna (Terumot 10:8): «The brine» of «a non-kosher fish is forbidden. Rabbi Yehuda says: A quarter-»log of non-kosher fish brine renders kosher food forbidden even if it is mixed «with two se’a» of permitted food, which is one hundred ninety-two times as much as a quarter-log.

segments.he: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל? שָׁאנֵי צִיר, דְּזֵיעָה בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: How can Rabbi Yehuda say that fish brine is nullified at all? «Doesn’t Rabbi Yehuda say» that «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type is not nullified?» The Gemara answers: «Brine is different because it is merely sweat,» i.e., it does not have the halakhic status of the fish itself.

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: הכא במאי עסקינן
moves.summary: Abaye answers a difficulty carried over from the previous unit by asking which case is under discussion.
moves.about: the teaching that a non-kosher egg imparts flavour applies only to an egg containing a chick

moves.cueHe: בביצת אפרוח, אבל טמאה – לא
moves.summary: Only an egg containing a chick imparts flavour; a plain non-kosher egg does not.

moves.cueHe: איתיביה
moves.summary: Rav Idi bar Avin objects from a baraita in which plain non-kosher eggs do impart flavour.
moves.about: whether an egg of a non-kosher bird without a chick imparts flavour to what is boiled with it

moves.cueHe: הכא נמי בביצת אפרוח
moves.summary: Abaye answers that the baraita too speaks of an egg with a chick, which is why it calls it non-kosher.
moves.about: the baraita too speaks of an egg containing a chick

moves.cueHe: והא מדקתני סיפא
moves.summary: The seifa's separate case of a chick implies the reisha has none, against Abaye.
moves.about: whether the baraita's first clause can be restricted to an egg containing a chick

moves.cueHe: פירושי קא מפרש
moves.summary: The seifa is not a second case but an explanation of the reisha.
moves.about: the baraita's latter clause explains the first rather than adding a separate ruling

moves.cueHe: הכי נמי מסתברא
moves.summary: Proof: on the other reading the seifa would be redundant a fortiori.
moves.about: supports reading the seifa as explanatory, since otherwise it is redundant

moves.cueHe: אי משום הא לא איריא
moves.summary: The redundancy proof is inconclusive: the seifa may have been taught to disclose the reisha.
moves.about: whether the redundancy argument proves the seifa merely explains the reisha

moves.cueHe: ההוא כזיתא תרבא דנפל בדיקולא דבשרא
moves.summary: An olive-bulk of forbidden fat falls into a pot of meat; Rav Asi would count what the pot absorbed.
moves.about: that the volume absorbed by the pot may be counted toward nullifying the forbidden fat

moves.cueHe: אטו דהיתרא בלע, דאיסורא לא בלע
moves.summary: The Rabbis object that the pot absorbed the forbidden fat no less than the permitted meat.
moves.about: whether the pot's absorption of permitted meat may be counted while its absorption of the forbidden fat is ignored

moves.cueHe: ההוא פלגא דזיתא דתרבא דנפל בדיקולא דבשרא
moves.summary: Half an olive-bulk of fat falls in; Mar bar Rav Ashi would nullify it in thirty half-measures.
moves.about: that a half-olive-bulk of forbidden fat is nullified in thirty half-olive-bulks rather than sixty

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אבוה: לאו אמינא לך
moves.summary: His father rebukes him not to treat measures lightly, and cites R. Yoḥanan that a half-measure is Torah-forbidden.
moves.about: whether rabbinic measures may be treated lightly so that half an olive-bulk needs only thirty times its volume

moves.cueHe: אמר רב שמן בר אבא
moves.summary: A six-link tradent chain from the house of the Nasi: an egg in sixty is forbidden, in sixty-one permitted.
moves.target: רב אידי בר אידי בר גרשם
moves.about: the ratio at which a non-kosher egg mixed with kosher eggs is nullified

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי זירא לרב שמן בר אבא: ראה שאתה מטיל בה גבול היתר
moves.summary: R. Zeira protests that Rav Shemen states as settled what the two greatest of the generation left unclarified.
moves.about: whether the sixty-one includes the forbidden egg itself — a point the two greatest of the generation left open

moves.cueHe: ואיבעיא להו
moves.summary: The unresolved dilemma: does 'sixty-one' count the forbidden egg itself or not?
moves.about: whether 'sixty-one' counts the forbidden egg itself or means sixty-one besides it

moves.cueHe: אתמר, אמר רבי חלבו אמר רב הונא
moves.summary: Rav Huna's formulation settles the count by adding 'and it' — sixty plus the forbidden egg.
moves.about: whether the sixty or sixty-one is counted together with the forbidden egg

moves.cueHe: ההוא דאתא לקמיה דרבן גמליאל בר רבי
moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel permits at forty-five, citing his father's forty-seven.
moves.about: the ratio at which Rabbi in fact permitted such a mixture

moves.cueHe: ההוא דאתא לקמיה דרבי שמעון בר רבי
moves.summary: R. Shimon bar Rabbi permits at forty-three, citing his father's forty-five.
moves.about: the ratio at which Rabbi in fact permitted such a mixture

moves.cueHe: ההוא דאתא לקמיה דרבי חייא
moves.summary: R. Ḥiyya dismisses a petitioner with: is there even thirty?
moves.about: whether the permitted food is even thirty times the volume of the forbidden

moves.cueHe: טעמא דליכא שלשים
moves.summary: R. Ḥiyya's wording implies thirty would suffice, against the sixty-fold standard.
moves.about: whether thirty times the volume suffices to nullify, against the accepted sixty

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חנינא: גוזמא
moves.summary: R. Ḥanina: it was hyperbole, not a measure.
moves.about: whether R. Ḥiyya's thirty sets a halakhic threshold

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא, אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי משום בר קפרא
moves.summary: All Torah prohibitions are nullified in sixty, in bar Kappara's name.
moves.about: the measure at which all Torah prohibitions are nullified

moves.cueHe: אמר לפניו רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק: רבי, אתה אומר כן
moves.summary: He counters with Rav Asi's version of the same chain: one hundred, not sixty.
moves.about: whether Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi in bar Kappara's name said sixty or one hundred

moves.cueHe: ושניהם לא למדוה אלא מזרוע בשלה
moves.summary: Both measures are derived from the nazirite's cooked foreleg.
moves.about: that his sixty-fold measure is derived only from the nazirite's cooked foreleg

moves.cueHe: דכתיב: ולקח הכהן את הזרוע בשלה
moves.summary: The verse and the baraita expounding בשלה are brought.
moves.about: that his hundred-fold measure is derived only from the nazirite's cooked foreleg

moves.cueHe: אין ״בשלה״ אלא שלימה
moves.summary: The first tanna: בשלה means the foreleg must be whole.
moves.about: what the verse's word בשלה specifies about the nazirite's foreleg

moves.cueHe: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי אומר: אין ״בשלה״ אלא שנתבשלה עם האיל
moves.summary: RaShBY: בשלה means it was cooked together with the ram.
moves.about: what the verse's word בשלה specifies about the nazirite's foreleg

moves.cueHe: דכולי עלמא בהדי איל מבשל לה
moves.summary: First construal of the dispute: all agree it is cooked with the ram; they differ on cutting before or after.
moves.about: that on his view one cuts the foreleg off and then cooks it with the ram

moves.cueHe: ואי בעית אימא
moves.summary: Second construal: all agree it is cut first; they differ on whether it is cooked with the ram or separately.
moves.about: an alternative account of what divides the first tanna and Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai

moves.cueHe: ללישנא קמא – אליבא דדברי הכל
moves.summary: On the first construal the derivation holds for all; on the second only for RaShBY.
moves.about: that on the second version the nullification measure can be derived from the foreleg only on his view

moves.cueHe: מאן דאמר בששים, סבר
moves.summary: Sixty reckons meat and bones together; one hundred reckons meat against meat.
moves.about: that his sixty reckons the foreleg's meat and bones against the ram's meat and bones

moves.cueHe: ומי ילפינן מינה? והתניא
moves.summary: A baraita's 'this is' seems to exclude all other prohibitions from the foreleg's rule.
moves.about: whether the general measures of nullification may be derived from the nazirite's foreleg at all

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: לא נצרכא אלא לרבי יהודה
moves.summary: Abaye: the emphasis is needed only against R. Yehuda's rule that like is not nullified in like.
moves.about: what the baraita's restrictive 'this is' excludes, if not the general measures of nullification

moves.cueHe: וליגמר מיניה
moves.summary: Then let R. Yehuda learn from the foreleg that like is nullified in like.
moves.about: why R. Yehuda does not learn from the foreleg that like mixed with like is nullified generally

moves.cueHe: גלי רחמנא ״ולקח מדם הפר ומדם השעיר״
moves.summary: The bull's and goat's bloods keep their names though mixed — like is not nullified in like.
moves.about: supplies R. Yehuda's defence: the two bloods keep their names though mixed, so like is not nullified in like

moves.cueHe: ומאי חזית דגמרינן מהאיך, ליגמר מהאי
moves.summary: Why prefer the bloods verse to the foreleg as the model?
moves.about: which of the two verses should be the source — the mixed bloods or the nazirite's foreleg

moves.cueHe: חדוש הוא, ומחדוש לא גמרינן
moves.summary: The foreleg is anomalous, and nothing is derived from an anomaly.
moves.about: the foreleg is a novelty and nothing general may be derived from it

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, למאה וששים נמי לא ליגמר
moves.summary: Then the sixty and hundred should not be derived from it either.
moves.about: whether calling the foreleg a novelty also blocks deriving the hundred- and sixty-fold measures from it

moves.cueHe: אטו אנן לקולא גמרינן
moves.summary: Those measures are learned only as a stringency, since Torah law nullifies by simple majority.
moves.about: the foreleg is used only to be stringent, since by Torah law a simple majority nullifies

moves.cueHe: רבא אמר: לא נצרכה אלא לטעם כעיקר
moves.summary: Rava: the emphasis is needed for טעם כעיקר, which in sacrificial food would forbid.
moves.about: what the baraita's restrictive 'this is' excludes

moves.cueHe: וליגמר מיניה
moves.summary: Then let sacrificial flavour be nullified as at the foreleg.
moves.about: why the nullification of sacrificial flavour is not derived from the nazirite's foreleg

moves.cueHe: גלי רחמנא גבי חטאת: ״כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש״
moves.summary: The sin-offering verse governs: what touches it takes on its status.
moves.about: the sin-offering verse, not the foreleg, governs the flavour of sacrificial food

moves.cueHe: ומאי חזית דגמרינן מהאיך, ליגמר מהאי
moves.summary: Why prefer the sin-offering verse to the foreleg?
moves.about: which verse should govern sacrificial flavour — the sin offering or the nazirite's foreleg

moves.cueHe: חדוש הוא, ומחדוש לא גמרינן
moves.summary: Again: the foreleg is anomalous.
moves.about: the foreleg is a novelty and nothing general may be derived from it

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, למאה וששים נמי לא ליגמר
moves.summary: Then the sixty and hundred should not be derived either.
moves.about: whether calling the foreleg a novelty also blocks deriving the hundred- and sixty-fold measures

moves.cueHe: אטו אנן לקולא קא גמרינן
moves.summary: Again: they are learned only as a stringency.
moves.about: the foreleg is used only to be stringent, since by Torah law a simple majority nullifies

moves.cueHe: רבינא אמר: לא נצרכה אלא למקום חתך
moves.summary: Ravina: the emphasis is needed for the place of the cut, forbidden elsewhere but permitted here.
moves.about: what the baraita's restrictive 'this is' excludes

moves.cueHe: יתיב רב דימי, וקאמר לה להא שמעתא
moves.summary: Rav Dimi recites the ruling that all prohibitions require one hundred.
moves.about: recites the ruling that all Torah prohibitions are nullified only in one hundred

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי: וכל איסורין שבתורה במאה? והתנן
moves.summary: Abaye objects from the mishna on leavening, flavouring and mixing teruma.
moves.about: whether all Torah prohibitions really require one hundred times their volume to be nullified

moves.cueHe: וקתני סיפא
moves.summary: He brings the following clause on split beans cooked with lentils.
moves.about: brings the mishna's following clause on split beans cooked with lentils

moves.cueHe: אין בהן להעלות במאה ואחד, אלא במאי? לאו בששים?
moves.summary: If not one hundred and one, then the beans must be nullified in sixty — against one hundred.
moves.about: in what quantity the teruma beans are nullified when there is not one hundred and one

moves.cueHe: לא, במאה
moves.summary: Rav Dimi: the mishna means one hundred, not sixty.
moves.about: in what quantity the teruma is nullified in the mishna's case

moves.cueHe: והא מדרישא במאה הוי, סיפא בששים
moves.summary: But the mishna contrasts its clauses, so if the reisha is one hundred the seifa must be sixty.
moves.about: whether both clauses of the mishna can speak of one hundred, given the contrast the mishna draws

moves.cueHe: רישא וסיפא במאה?
moves.summary: Would you have both clauses stating one hundred?
moves.about: the contrast between the mishna's clauses shows the seifa cannot also mean one hundred

moves.cueHe: לא, רישא במאה וחד, וסיפא במאה
moves.summary: Rav Dimi distinguishes: the reisha is one hundred and one, the seifa one hundred.
moves.about: how the two clauses of the mishna are to be distinguished

moves.cueHe: וכי יש בו כדי לחמץ במאה וחד, אמאי לא בטיל?
moves.summary: Could leaven still leaven dough one hundred and one times its volume? Then why is it not nullified?
moves.about: whether leaven could still leaven dough one hundred and one times its volume rather than being nullified

moves.cueHe: אישתיק
moves.summary: Rav Dimi is silent and the difficulty stands.
moves.about: Rav Dimi has no answer and the difficulty about leaven in one hundred and one stands against him

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: דלמא שאני שאור דחימוצו קשה
moves.summary: Abaye supplies the answer himself: leaven's potency is exceptional.
moves.about: whether leaven is a special case whose leavening power is potent enough to act at one hundred and one

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אדכרתן מילתא דאמר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
moves.summary: Reminded, Rav Dimi cites R. Yosei b. R. Ḥanina: the measures are not uniform — brine needs near two hundred.
moves.about: adduces R. Yosei b. R. Ḥanina's rule that the measures of nullification are not uniform

moves.cueHe: והאמר רבי יהודה: מין במינו לא בטיל
moves.summary: But R. Yehuda holds like is never nullified in like — how then is brine nullified at all?
moves.about: how R. Yehuda can allow fish brine to be nullified when he holds like is never nullified in like

moves.cueHe: שאני ציר, דזיעה בעלמא הוא
moves.summary: Brine is mere exudate, not the fish itself, so it is nullified even in its own kind.
moves.about: brine is different because it is mere exudate and not the fish itself
